FIRMWARE V1.2

1. OVERVIEW

Time Slice has four Tracks each with a separate audio input and output. Audio is recorded to individual buffers, which can be played back and manipulated to their track outputs.

Additionally the Tracks can be mixed to the Stereo Mix output via the TRS MIX OUT jack.

Tracks can also receive audio from other track outputs or the Mix Output for resampling or recording a live performance based on the other tracks.

Each track has its own FX Chain that includes a low latency Pitch Shifter, Tilt Filter, Delay line, Wave Folder, Decimator and Reverb.

Time Slice can use Internal Clock sync (recommended), External Clock sync, or MIDI Clock sync.

The Loop and Delay units can be quantised time (based on the tempo) or unquantised time in milliseconds.

When using quantised Loop time, the LOOP and REC Button presses are quantised to the nearest 1/8th beat.

Each track has Trigger Inputs/Output and CV Modulation inputs that can be routed to a choice of destinations such as Record, Loop, Filter, Delay-time, Pitch Shift, Loop Splice Number, Restart, Reverse, etc etc.

MIDI CCs can be used as modulation sources, and MIDI NOTE data can be used as means to play loops as 1-shot samples polyphonically.

4. LOOPING

To use the Looping functions, the internal or external clock needs to be running, this is indicated by a flashing Green LED ● next to the S/S button.

Press the S/S Button ● to start the internal clock ( recommended ), or use a running external Clock.

4.1 LOOP STYLES

There are three ways of enabling Loops on Time Slice, RETROSPECTIVE, BOSS and DAW style. (see the diagram on page 5)

The Loop Styles RETRO, or BOSS can be chosen in the Settings menu. ( see Settings Menu )

- RETROSPECIVE

The endpoint of the loop is defined by when the LOOP Button ● is pressed, and the start point is the moment back in time previously defined by the Loop Length.

In the Track menu (TRK) navigate to the LOOP UNIT item, and adjust the setting to QUANTISED, to use tempo based time divisions.

Then navigate to LOOP and adjust the length of the Loop, say to 2 bars.

Now press the REC Button to start recording, and perform some music or sound, When you are happy with the last two bars, press the LOOP Button ● to engage the Loop.

NB when using quantised Loop units, the LOOP Button activations are always quantised to the nearest 1/8 beat, so you will need to think about the timings of when to set the loop.

The Retrospective Loop style allows the user to perform and record repeated phrases continuously, and when happy with a phrase, Loop can be engaged to capture the last phrase played.

Try engaging the Metronome (hold the MUTE Button ●, and press the S/S Button ●) to get a feel for the Bar divisions for beat based loops when performing.

The Metronome plays every 1/4 beat, so 1 bar is represented by 4 Metronome blips. For example if making a 1 bar loop, hit the LOOP Button on the 5th Metronome blip after playing 1 bar of music or audio.

- BOSS

With BOSS Loop style the Loop length is defined by the time between pressing the REC Button ●, and then the LOOP Button ●.

To make a BOSS style loop, change the LOOP STYLE menu setting to BOSS, make sure the clock is running.

Press the REC Button ●, perform some sound, then when finished press the LOOP button ● to create the loop.

Again, if using quantised loop units, these button presses are quantised to the nearest 1/8 beat

pages.title: Page 9
pages.content:
A Slice is a shorter piece of a recorded Loop or Loaded audio.

Slices are normally loop length based, but alternatively that can be based on markers placed in the audio. ( see SLICE MODE in Track Menu below )

Once a length of audio has been recorded or Loaded, in the Track menu adjust the LOOP length to a shorter length than the original, to play smaller sections of the audio, called SLICES.

The menu parameter SLICE is the Slice number that you will hear when a track is playing the new shorter loop.

Using Loop Length based slices for example, record a 4 Bar length Loop then adjust the Loop Length to 1/2 Bar, the Slice range will be 1-8, allowing you to select 1 of 8 Slices from the original loop.

Slice number 1 is is the first slice of the looped audio, and represents the beginning of the original loop.

Selecting negative Loop slices -1, -2, -3, etc., will jump back in time.

This is great if you want to play several variations of the same phrase and after setting the Loop, you can go back in time and jump to these different versions of the phrases.

Or you can go micro, and scan through the looped audio in very small loop sizes, like the technique of Granular synthesis.

Try this with a piece of longer looped audio (2 bars or more) then set the Loop length to a short value, such as 1/32 or 100ms, then scroll through the SLICE numbers to hear this Granular scanning technique.

You can also use a CV to scan through the buffer. (see EXAMPLE USES FOR MODULATION INPUTS)

If you have a tempo synced break beat loop of 2 bars or so, you can set your loop length to something shorter like ¼ or even 1/8 bar, and use the SLICE number to jump around to different parts in the break beat, much like the way drum-and-bass music is made.

Try LOADing the Track “break_beats_100bpm.wav” from the internal memory and adjusting the Loop length to ¼ bar, then adjust the SLICE number to hear the individual slices playback.

Slices can also be modulated with CV or MIDI, for highly creative restructuring of audio loops. (see Modulation Menu)

4.3 LOOP MODES

In addition to the normal Loop Mode, there are two other types of Loop Modes; 1-SHOT and LIVE.

In the Track menu, navigate to LOOP MODE, to select.

- 1-SHOT
This mode acts more like a traditional sampler, where the Loop plays just once then stops. To use this mode either LOAD a WAV sample or record a loop in the normal way.
Playback is triggered by a RESET trigger to a TRIG input, or MIDI CC, or MIDI NOTE (see Modulation Menu)
You can also manually trigger playback by holding the TRACK Button ●, and pressing the S/S Button ●.
The XFADE value acts as a decay amount fading the level of the playback towards the end of the sample. [ 0 – no fade, 50% - the sample fades from halfway to the end ]
1-SHOT normally plays to the end of the loop, but this can be changed to GATED mode where the sample stops playing when the gate level turns off. ( see 1-SHOT in Settings Menu )

- 1-SHOT POLY
This mode is the same as 1-SHOT but enables four individual voices of polyphonic playback, this can be great to use with a MIDI keyboard, or for creating complex layers of overlapping samples.

- LIVE
This mode creates a looping buffer behind the record head of the main buffer, much like a live single-grain granular effect.
With the clock running, press the LOOP Button to engage looping, then activate Record by pressing the TRACK Button and REC Button.
The contents of the loop are only updated by a SLICE value change, or RESET trigger via a TRIG input, or MIDI CC etc.
You can also manually trigger the loop update by holding the TRACK Button ●, and pressing the S/S Button ●.
It is a great tool to create glitch or stutter effects from live audio input.
(See EXAMPLE USES FOR MODULATION INPUTS)

5. MENU

5.1 TRACK MENU

The Track Menu is where all the Loop orientated settings of a track can be adjusted. The settings apply to the currently active track, indicated by the the Green LED ● under the TRACK Button.

Press and hold the MOD Button to adjust the dry/wet MIX of the Reverb.

- FILTER – This is the cutoff frequency of the HP/LP tilt filter.

This is a classic DJ style tilt filter, where adjusting the cutoff frequency passes the mode from Low Pass to High Pass mode.

Hold the SHIFT Button and dial the JOG Wheel to adjust the resonance amount. (NB high settings of resonance may create saturation-distortion when used with the DELAY effect)

To reduce muddiness in DELAY or REVERB effects, try setting the FILTER HP frequency to a low value such as 100-200, eliminating some of the lower frequencies for a cleaner effect.

For increasingly warmer DELAY effect repeats, try setting to a LP frequency value such as 2khz to reduce the high frequencies in the delay feedback path.

- WAVE FOLD – This applies a Wave Fold / Saturation type effect to the audio.

Larger values create an unusual distortion effect. Sounds good on bass drums, and simple pitched sounds.

- AMP – Here you can add additional gain to the signal, which can be useful for low level sounds.

Use the JOG wheel to adjust the ratio such as 1:4, hold the MOD button ● and use the JOG Wheel to adjust the Threshold, hold the SHIFT button to allowing adjusting the Makeup gain.

5.3 SETTINGS MENU

This menu is used for adjusting the Global settings of the Time Slice module, as well as some Track based settings such as Input Source etc,

- BPM – When using the internal Clock, this allows the tempo to be adjusted. When using an external clock source, the detected tempo is displayed here.

- TAP BPM – When using the internal Clock, the tempo can be set by tapping the MOD Button to a consistent 1/4 beat for 4 beats or more.
If recording from a beat based source such as a drum break, it can be useful to use the Tap Tempo to get the tempo matched before recording. Set the Metronome on (press Mute and S/S) and start tapping, using the S/S button to restart the clock to see if the Metronome blips match the beat of the music.

- INPUT – Here you can choose the audio input Level or Source, for the currently selected track.
For the Audio Input jack, the level can be chosen from LINE Level, EURO-rack level, or HOT EURO level. (HOT EURO is for signals that are greater than a +/- 6V range)
This value is per track, the track number is indicated in the top right corner.
Please make sure to select the correct level to avoid a CLIP ! overload of the signal.
NB the Track Inputs are normalised from Left to Right, so be aware that a track that is not set to the correct level may still clip even without a jack in it's input.
Alternatively the audio input can be taken from the output of another track, or the Mix Output, enabling resampling of tracks.
This is similar to the four-track tape technique known as track bouncing, where existing tracks are mixed and recorded to another track.

- LOOPSTYL – Select the Loop Style from RETROspective or BOSS for loop recording.

- RSET TRK – Use this option to reset the currently selected track parameters to the default settings. This resets all the track, modulation and FX parameters.
Select "YES" and press the JOG Wheel for a 1sec.
You can also select RESET ALL, to reset all the tracks !!

- INPT MON – The Input Monitor option toggles On/Off the preview of the audio input, which is mixed to the currently selected track.

- METRNOME - The Metronome can be turned ON/OFF and it's output can be set to ACTIVE TRACK / ALL TRACKS / OUT1 / OUT2 /. OUT3 / OUT4.
NB the Metronome ca also be turned On or Off by holding the MUTE button and pressing the S/S button.

- 1-SHOT – This allows setting the gate mode of the 1-SHOT loop mode. NORMAL plays the whole loop when triggered, GATED plays the loop until the gate signal goes low.

5.4 MODULATION MENU

This Modulation Menu is where you can assign modulation CVs from the M1,M2 inputs, & MIDI CCs to destinations such as Speed, Pitch Shift, Slice, Feedback etc. Also the T1, T2 trigger inputs and MIDI CCs can be assigned to events such as Reset, Record, Reverse, Mute etc.

The T1 jacks can also be used as a trigger outputs for End of Loop Pulses, and Transient detect pulses.

The Clock IN jack can be used as a MIDI INPUT for modulation if not using External Clock.

Press the MOD Button to access the Modulation Menu, use the JOG Wheel to select a Modulation Source such as MOD1 (the top menu item in bold). Then press the JOG Wheel to toggle to the parameter edit, and select a modulation destination.

NB The destination will ONLY become active when you press the JOG Wheel again to escape to the top level of the Modulation Menu. (MOD1, MOD2 etc in bold)

MOD1, MOD2 – Here you can route a CV from the M1 or M2 inputs to a destination parameter for the selected track.

The trimmer below the M1 socket is an attenuator for the M1 CV.

If MOD1 is selected, and no Jack is inserted into the M1 socket, the attenuator acts as a control knob for this parameter. This can be useful for setting up manual controls for certain parameters.

5.4 MODULATION MENU

TRIG1 OUT – The T1 jacks can also be used as trigger outputs for EOP (end-of-loop pulse), and TRANS transient detection pulse.

The TRANS80 and TRANS50 options send a brief pulse out when the audio level of the track exceeds 80% or 50% of it's average value.

EOP will send a brief pulse out each time the track's loop reaches it's end and restarts.

The EOP pulse can also be clock multiplied or divided, creating multiple pulses per loop like a clock, or periodically every 2,3rd, 4th etc loop.

Hold the MOD button and adjust the division or multiplication ratio with the JOG Wheel.

MIDI NOTE – This allows the use of MIDI NOTES to trigger the Reset of the Loop for 1-SHOT style sample playback, and use the NOTE value to control the pitch of the loop via Speed, or Pitch Shift.

Alternatively the NOTE value can be used to select Slices within the loop. This can be used for playing multi-samples within a WAV file, where each note or hit is aligned either with a marker in the file, or aligned to BPM time divisions such as 1/2 bar intervals.

( see Examples below )

MIDI CC a-d – There are four assignable modulation slots for MIDI CC's for each track.

Hold the SHIFT Button, and press the JOG Wheel to enable MIDI Learn for the selected MIDI CC modulation slot. The number of the CC will flash on the top right corner whilst the MIDI Learn is active.

You can also choose the CC number by holding the SHIFT Button and dialling in the JOG Wheel.

Live Granular Buffer [ Live Loop ]

in the Track Menu menu set the LOOP MODE to LIVE.

Make sure the clock is running.

Set the LOOP length to a short value such as 1/32 or 1/16 etc.

Press the LOOP Button to activate the loop, then press the REC Button to activate recording.

In the Modulation Menu, select TRIG1 and set the destination to RST.

Connect a random or periodic pulse signal to the T1 input of the selected track.

Each time the track receives a high pulse on the T1 input, the Loop will be updated with the incoming audio.

You can even create a live reversed audio effect, by reversing the loop (hold the SHIFT Button and press the MUTE Button )

Quantised Record overdubbing to create rhythmic sound patterns

Set a track's LOOP UNIT to QUANTISED, and set the Loop length to 2 bars.

Start the clock, using the S/S button, and press the LOOP button to engage the loop.

In the Modulation menu, navigate to TRIG1, and select REC. Hold the MOD button and using the JOG wheel adjust the quantised parameter to Q1/16. Remember to toggle back up to the top level of the menu to applying the setting.

Connect a randomly varying voltage, or random trigger trigger signal to the T1 input jack, you should start to see the REC LED flashing on and off, indicating the record status. If it is nearly always on, adjust the speed or level of your random source to a slower / lower setting.

Connect a sound source that you can easily manipulate the the frequency and timbre, such as the ALGO module, to the track Audio Input, and begin to play with the timbre and frequency controls.

Each time the Record gets triggered little bits of sound begin to get recorded into the loop, because these are quantised in time the sounds will feel quite rhythmic as they build up.

Try occasionally turning off the sound source, to create silent gaps within the loop.
